statement: The function returns a result r and r = min { Σ_{i=1}^{n} ceil(power[m_i] / i) | (m_1,...,m_n) is a permutation of {0,...,n-1} }, where for positive integers a and b, ceil(a/b) is the smallest integer d ≥ 0 such that d*b ≥ a. Here the index i is the 1-based position in the kill order (the gain when attempting to kill the i-th monster is i).
preconditions: Let n = len(power). Assume 1 ≤ n ≤ 17 and 1 ≤ power[j] ≤ 10^9 for all 0 ≤ j < n.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, there exists a permutation (m_1,...,m_n) of {0,...,n-1} such that r = Σ_{i=1}^{n} ceil(power[m_i] / i), where ceil(a/b) is the smallest integer d ≥ 0 such that d*b ≥ a.
preconditions: Let n = len(power). Assume 1 ≤ n ≤ 17 and 1 ≤ power[j] ≤ 10^9 for all 0 ≤ j < n.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, for every permutation (m_1,...,m_n) of {0,...,n-1}, r ≤ Σ_{i=1}^{n} ceil(power[m_i] / i), where ceil(a/b) is the smallest integer d ≥ 0 such that d*b ≥ a.
preconditions: Let n = len(power). Assume 1 ≤ n ≤ 17 and 1 ≤ power[j] ≤ 10^9 for all 0 ≤ j < n.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, r ≥ n.
preconditions: Let n = len(power). Assume 1 ≤ n ≤ 17 and 1 ≤ power[j] ≤ 10^9 for all 0 ≤ j < n.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, r ≥ Σ_{i=1}^{n} ceil(m / i), where ceil(a/b) is the smallest integer d ≥ 0 such that d*b ≥ a.
preconditions: Let n = len(power). Assume 1 ≤ n ≤ 17 and 1 ≤ power[j] ≤ 10^9 for all 0 ≤ j < n. Let m = min_{0≤j<n} power[j].

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, r ≥ Σ_{j=0}^{n-1} ceil(power[j] / n), where ceil(a/b) is the smallest integer d ≥ 0 such that d*b ≥ a.
preconditions: Let n = len(power). Assume 1 ≤ n ≤ 17 and 1 ≤ power[j] ≤ 10^9 for all 0 ≤ j < n.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, r = power[0].
preconditions: Let n = len(power). Assume n = 1 and 1 ≤ power[0] ≤ 10^9.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, r = Σ_{i=1}^{n} ceil(c / i), where ceil(a/b) is the smallest integer d ≥ 0 such that d*b ≥ a.
preconditions: Let n = len(power). Assume 1 ≤ n ≤ 17 and there exists an integer c with 1 ≤ c ≤ 10^9 such that power[j] = c for all 0 ≤ j < n.

statement: Whenever minimum_time(power) returns r and minimum_time(power') returns r', we have r = r'.
preconditions: Let n = len(power). Assume 1 ≤ n ≤ 17 and 1 ≤ power[j] ≤ 10^9 for all 0 ≤ j < n. Let σ be any permutation of {0,...,n-1} and define power' of length n by power'[i] = power[σ(i)] for 0 ≤ i < n.

statement: Whenever minimum_time(power) returns r and minimum_time(q) returns r_q, we have r ≤ r_q.
preconditions: Let n = len(power). Assume 1 ≤ n ≤ 17 and 1 ≤ power[j] ≤ 10^9 for all 0 ≤ j < n. Let q be any array of length n such that 1 ≤ q[j] ≤ 10^9 and power[j] ≤ q[j] for all 0 ≤ j < n.

statement: The function returns a result r (it does not panic, overflow, or otherwise fail).
preconditions: Let n = len(power). Assume 1 ≤ n ≤ 17 and 1 ≤ power[j] ≤ 10^9 for all 0 ≤ j < n.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, there exists a permutation (m_1,...,m_n) of {0,...,n-1} such that power[m_1] ≤ power[j] for all 0 ≤ j < n, and r = Σ_{i=1}^{n} ceil(power[m_i] / i), where ceil(a/b) is the smallest integer d ≥ 0 such that d*b ≥ a.
preconditions: Let n = len(power). Assume 1 ≤ n ≤ 17 and 1 ≤ power[j] ≤ 10^9 for all 0 ≤ j < n.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, r = (n - 1) + ceil(P / n), where ceil(a/b) is the smallest integer d ≥ 0 such that d*b ≥ a.
preconditions: Let n = len(power). Assume 1 ≤ n ≤ 17 and there exists an index k and an integer P with 2 ≤ P ≤ 10^9 such that power[k] = P and power[j] = 1 for all j ≠ k.
